summary: Join our training course to understand how economic trends shape monetary policy. Gain valuable insights and practical skills for effective decision-making.
lede: Global economic trends shape monetary policy through inflation, interest rates, exchange rates and capital flows. The course is for central bank staff, government economists, financial sector teams and investment professionals who need to interpret policy signals and inform decisions. Participants practise filtering economic data, assessing how policy moves affect credit and prices, and linking global shocks to exchange-rate pressures and policy scenarios.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who operate at the intersection of global economic trends and local policy decisions, equipping them with the tools to navigate complex monetary landscapes.
audience: Central bank staff and financial sector regulators
Bank treasury, ALM, risk, and research teams
Government economists, planners, and budget officers
Corporate finance leaders, CFOs, and strategy teams
Trade, procurement, and supply chain managers exposed
Development finance and project finance teams
Policy advisors, think tanks, and research professionals
modules: The Global Macro Picture and Why Monetary Policy Reacts
Reading Growth, Inflation, and Labour Signals Without Noise
Global Inflation Drivers: Energy, Food, Supply Chains, Wages, Expectations
The Central Bank Reaction Function: How Decisions Are Really Made
Interest Rates, Yield Curves, and Market Expectations as Early Signals
Exchange Rates, Capital Flows, and External Vulnerability
Monetary Policy Transmission: From Policy Rate to Credit, Prices, and Jobs
Liquidity, Financial Stability, and Macroprudential Linkages
Scenario Planning and Stress Testing for Policy and Strategy
Policy Communication and Credibility: Statements, Forward Guidance, and Trust
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of macroeconomic principles and experience in financial decision-making roles. Familiarity with economic data and policy analysis is beneficial.
